chunks: 1866 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
He was asked about regurgitation: “Does it invalidate the fast of the fasting person?” He said: “No.”

There is no harm in rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose for the fasting person. When he rinses his mouth and nose, he should not swallow his saliva until he spits three times; and if he rinses his mouth and water enters his throat, then if that was for the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer), there is no make-up fast upon him.

key_terms.الْقَلَسِ: regurgitation or reflux rising to the mouth during fasting
key_terms.قَضَاءَ: make-up of the fast due after invalidation

ai.seo_question: Does regurgitation or rinsing the mouth invalidate the fast in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings related to fasting. It states that regurgitation does not invalidate the fast, and it also clarifies the ruling of rinsing the mouth and nose during fasting, including the case where water reaches the throat during wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer).
